cards: Xuanzang was a Chinese Buddhist monk, scholar and traveller who journeyed overland to India between 629 and 645 to collect scriptures.
Samo was a Frankish merchant who, according to the Chronicle of Fredegar, led the Slavs of Central Europe in a revolt against the Avars around 623 and was then chosen as their king, ruling for some…
Harsha, or Harshavardhana, was the most famous ruler of the Pushyabhuti dynasty, reigning from 606 to 647 from Thanesar and Kannauj over much of northern India.
Penda was the pagan king of Mercia who made it the strongest kingdom of the English Midlands in the mid-7th century.
Kubrat was a Bulgar ruler of the Dulo clan who, in the 630s, threw off Avar or Turkic overlordship and united the Onogur, Bulgar and related tribes of the steppe north of the Black Sea into Old…
Amr ibn al-As was an Arab commander and companion of the Prophet Muhammad.
Pulakeshin II was the greatest king of the Chalukyas of Badami, in the western Deccan.
Saint Gall was a missionary monk, traditionally said to be an Irish companion of Saint Columbanus, who around 612 settled as a hermit in the Steinach valley south of Lake Constance.
Emperor Taizong, born Li Shimin, was the second emperor of the Tang Dynasty (r. 626–649).
Oswald was king of Northumbria from 634 to 642.
Edwin of Northumbria was king of Deira and Bernicia from 616 and the most powerful ruler in England of his day.
Emperor Yang was the second emperor of the Sui dynasty.
Emperor Gaozu, born Li Yuan, was the founder of the Tang Dynasty.
founded dynasty 618 CE · Central & East Asia
Narasimhavarman I, known as Mamalla, 'great wrestler', was king of the Pallava dynasty from about 630 to 668.
Asparuh was the founder of the First Bulgarian Empire on the lower Danube.
Cadwallon ap Cadfan was a king of Gwynedd who, allied with Penda of Mercia, defeated and killed Edwin of Northumbria at the Battle of Hatfield Chase in 633.
Mahendravarman I was king of the Pallava dynasty of Kanchipuram in the early 7th century.
Sambandar, Thirugnana Sambandar, was a Tamil Shaiva poet-saint of the 7th century, one of the most revered of the Nayanars.
Shahrbaraz was a leading Sasanian general under Khosrow II.
d. 630 CE · Islamic Caliphates & Middle East
Uqba ibn Nafi was an Arab general of the Rashidun and Umayyad caliphates who led the conquest of North Africa.
Yeon Gaesomun was a Goguryeo general and statesman who seized power in a coup in 642, killing King Yeongnyu and placing King Bojang on the throne while ruling as military dictator.
Appar, also called Tirunavukkarasar, was a Tamil Shaiva poet-saint of the seventh century and one of the most revered of the 63 Nayanars.
Ceolfrith (c. 642–716) was abbot of the twin monastery of Wearmouth–Jarrow from 688 and the teacher of Bede.
Dagobert I was a Merovingian king of the Franks, made king of Austrasia in 623 and ruler of all the Frankish kingdoms from 629 until his death in 639.
Muyeol, born Kim Chunchu, was king of Silla from 654 to 661, the first king from the 'true bone' rank.
Pippin of Herstal was mayor of the palace of Austrasia and, after his victory over Neustria at Tertry in 687, the real ruler of the whole Frankish kingdom under figurehead Merovingian kings.
Shashanka was a king of Gauda in Bengal in the late 6th and early 7th centuries, often described as the first ruler to unite much of Bengal.
Chlothar II was a Merovingian king, son of Chilperic I and Fredegund, who became King of Neustria as an infant in 584.
Cædwalla was king of Wessex from about 685 to 688.
Justinian II was a Byzantine emperor of the Heraclian dynasty who reigned from 685 to 695 and again from 705 to 711.
Khosrow II was the last great king of the Sasanian Empire, reigning in the late sixth and early seventh centuries CE.
r. 590–628 CE · Islamic Caliphates & Middle East
Kim Yu-sin was a Silla general descended from the royal house of Geumgwan Gaya, his great-grandfather being its last king, Guhyeong.
Saint Cuthbert was a Northumbrian monk and bishop of Lindisfarne, the most venerated saint of northern England.
Songtsen Gampo was the emperor who built the Tibetan Empire in the early 7th century, ruling until 649 with Lhasa as his capital.
Aldhelm was an Anglo-Saxon scholar, poet and churchman, abbot of Malmesbury and from 705 the first bishop of Sherborne.
Birinus was a missionary bishop sent from Rome by Pope Honorius I who converted the West Saxons.
Gar Tongtsen Yulsung was chief minister of the Tibetan Empire under Songtsen Gampo and, after his death, effective regent for the young Mangsong Mangtsen.
Khalid ibn al-Walid was an Arab military commander of the early Islamic period, celebrated as one of the most successful generals of his age.
d. 642 CE · Islamic Caliphates & Middle East
Peada was a son of Penda of Mercia, made ruler of the Middle Angles around 653.
Prince Shōtoku (574–622) was a regent and statesman of the Yamato court in Japan under Empress Suiko.
